transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-04
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Desai (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Mark Chu, Alicia Park (BlueLeaf)
---
Summary (auto): quick readiness pass; Triaged two blockers (SSO and kv-cache priming); outlined next steps for canary.
---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody thanks for joining, um quick agenda — status on infra creds, staging gateway replay, bench numbers and next steps.
[00:15] Lena: yeah thanks. we made some progress on the peering side, still waiting on the route table to land, should be in by tomorrow. Mark's on that.
[00:22] Mark: yes route table update in progress, valve — uh I mean the route rules, sorry, I'm running it through our infra CD.
[00:29] Priya: cool. on our side I ran a surface-level connectivity check yesterday from the private control plane; we saw TLS handshake succeed but one flow had intermittent 502s during large payloads — might be MTU or the gateway health-check config.
[00:45] Mark: that tracks, we have jumbo frames disabled in staging, so maybe PMTU is smaller; will align with network team.
[00:52] Alicia: also we need to confirm the SSO timing, we want users to hit the staging gateway with SSO enabled for canary. where are we on SAML metadata?
[01:00] Jordan: Lena — you were going to share the IdP metadata file?
[01:04] Lena: yes, we'll send SAML metadata today; one note our IdP team wants to test with a single test user first, not wide rollout.
[01:12] Priya: that's fine, Redwood supports test binding. small caveat: our console shows the S-S-O config status but in earlier exports the attribute mappings were reshuffled — sometimes 'employee_id' gets transcribed as 'empl‑id' in the mapping docs, so double-check attributes when you send them.
[01:29] Jordan: thanks Priya. next, kv‑cache warmup: Priya can you explain the warmup plan and why it's needed?
[01:36] Priya: sure. the model we're serving uses long contexts and heavy KV hits, so cold start latency spiked to ~450ms p99 in the initial bench. Warmup fills the KV cache with recent prefixes to reduce median/99p for the first few requests. It is a small batch job against the model keys; we'll run it during low-traffic window. note: there's a small chance of increased egress cost if you run excessive warmups in multiple clusters.
[02:05] Lena: what's the expected improvement? numbers?
[02:08] Priya: based on our bench, warmup reduced p99 from ~450ms to ~160ms for the selected prompt set; median improved from 85ms to 60ms. I'll add the exact histograms to the sheet.
[02:21] Jordan: we'll attach the bench sheet link — https://redwood.example.com/poc/blueleaf-bench — has raw traces and the quant profiles we tried.
[02:30] Mark: slight concern on cost — does the warmup keep cache entries indefinitely? how does eviction work?
[02:36] Priya: eviction is LRU with windowed TTL; you can tune TTL per workload. Also there's an option to pin a small set of prefixes for canary. That adds memory but is cheap compared to token cost.
[02:50] Alicia: timeline for running warmup before canary?
[02:53] Priya: we recommend 1 hour warmup for initial canary traffic at low TPS, then periodic refresh every 6 hours if traffic is bursty.
[03:03] Jordan: switching to SLOs — BlueLeaf mentioned wanting 99p under 200ms and median under 100ms for the in-app agent flows. Is that still the target?
[03:13] Lena: yes, but for long context searches we can accept 250ms p99 for the first iteration.
[03:18] Jordan: understood, we'll document 200ms as target for critical flows and 250ms as acceptable for long-context batched flows.
[03:25] Priya: one more perf note: we ran a quantized config (int8) which dropped token cost ~28% but bumped p99 by ~30ms. Tradeoff is obvious — we'll surface both variants in the sheet.
[03:40] Mark: any security review items outstanding? audit logs?
[03:44] Jordan: we sent the SOC2 + security whitepaper earlier; you asked about longer audit retention, that is an add-on feature and we can propose retention options as a follow-up.
[03:53] Lena: good. also we need the gateway to log request ids to your tracing so we can join traces with our Datadog. is that feasible?
[03:59] Priya: yes, we can emit request_id headers and open a small tracing hook. we'll coordinate with Mark on the expected tag names.
[04:08] Jordan: ok, blockers summary: (1) SSO metadata handoff (customer) (2) route table and MTU check (customer) (3) KV warmup and run in staging (Redwood) (4) attach traces and logs (both). Anything else?
[04:20] Alicia: can we also test failure fallback — like if the dedicated pool is saturated can requests fall back to a cheaper hosted variant? we want to validate graceful degradation.
[04:30] Priya: yes Redwood supports routing fallback — you can define a fallback model (smaller or quantized) and automatic policy. We'll demo that in the canary run and include recovery windows.
[04:40] Mark: from SRE side, throttling rules and circuit breaker thresholds would be good to see prior to canary.
[04:46] Jordan: we'll include the policy defaults and propose thresholds; action item for Jordan to send suggested thresholds.
[04:52] Lena: last question — how do we handle data retention for inference logs in private deployment? we need KMS/HSM integration notes.
[04:59] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM options; we have docs and an integration checklist. I'll attach the checklist to the ticket after the call.
[05:09] Jordan: awesome. let's recap next steps and owners. Priya will run the warmup and share logs; Jordan will update bench sheet and thresholds; Lena/Mark will send SAML and route updates. We'll reconvene next Thursday to validate the canary gate.
[05:25] Alicia: works for us. thanks all.
[05:30] [crosstalk] Jordan: thanks everyone, bye.
